summary: Chelan County site of an L-4 cab lookout in place by 1934, removed or destroyed in 1959; now reached only on foot from Stehekin, with no remains described.

facts.design: L-4 cab (the Forest Fire Lookout Association list calls the site ground; WillhiteWeb mentions a tower and storm cellar)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1959; Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows the site as Ground Gone; no source describes what remains

staffing.status: John Wilbur Boehm in the 1930s; Jim Berry in 1938 and 1939 (WillhiteWeb text; its photo captions say Brockman); emergency station manned in July 1930

access.note: Reached on foot by trail from Stehekin Landing; no road access. No closure or permit rule in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No lookout stands. The Purple Creek trail from Stehekin Landing runs 8 miles to Purple Pass, and the site is about half a mile past the pass.

events.note: Emergency station at Boulder Butte manned, per a July 1930 Wenatchee newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts
L-4 cab in place by September 1934 (WillhiteWeb); register says built in the 1930s
Jim Berry was lookout in 1938 and 1939 while attending college (WillhiteWeb)
Register says removed; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed
Registered August 20, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1959; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed that year. The story reports both and does not choose between them.
The Forest Fire Lookout Association list calls the site Ground, while WillhiteWeb mentions a tower and a storm cellar beneath it. No source gives a tower height, so the story says cab only.
WillhiteWeb gives 8 miles. Wenatchee Outdoors puts Purple Pass 8 miles from the trailhead, with the site another half mile on. The story uses the Wenatchee figures.
WillhiteWeb's text names Jim Berry; its photo captions for 1938 and 1939 read Lookout Brockman. The story gives Berry as the text's name and reports the caption conflict.

notes_for_editor: Firelookout.com's 3 miles is a direct distance from Stehekin, while the trail is 8 miles or more; both are reported as written. The register and Firelookout.com disagree on 1959 (removed vs destroyed). WillhiteWeb's 2022 photos are not described in its text, so no present-day remains are confirmed. Register photos are credited to Paul Boehm with no license, so none were added.
